title: Task arithmetic versus shared task-vector Mirror basis
hypothesis: A shared task-delta basis with compact Mirror coordinates can reconstruct and compose task functions at lower bytes and less interference than raw independent task vectors; PCA/SVD and ordinary coefficient controls may explain the result.
physical_object: one shared base linear model and task-delta basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task/combination coefficient address over basis vectors
logical_multiplicity: multiple task edits and held-out compositions

development.allowed: validate held-out task split, composition rules, interference and exact payload bytes

storage.authority: actual serialized base+basis+codes or raw vectors

success_gate: Held-out task and composition NRMSE <=0.05 with <=70% bytes vs raw vectors; Mirror-specific claim requires beating PCA/generic coefficient control at matched bytes.
failure_gate: Held-out NRMSE >0.20, composition interference >0.25, or generic coefficients match Mirror.
boundaries: Combination count is not independent capacity
